pr_title: Hide the "Details" link of commit status when the user cannot access actions
pr_body: Fix #26685 If a commit status comes from Gitea Actions and the user cannot access the repo's actions unit (the user does not have the permission or the actions unit is disabled), a 404 page will occur after clicking the "Details" link. We should hide the "Details" link in this case.
pr_comments: Can this be hidden in SQL query?

> Can this be hidden in SQL query?

🤔 Are you saying that we shouldn't select `TargetURL` in the SQL query if the user doesn't have a read permission for actions? 
It's feasible. The problem is that there are multiple functions related to query submission status. I'm worried that modifying them will bring too many changes to the callers of these functions. (In fact, I've made changes to a series of functions that need to query the commit status. So now I'm not sure which is the better solution)
Since it is only a UI bug (404), which doesn't block daily usage, I think it is very trivial and doesn't need to backport. Too many lines are touched and we should avoid unnecessary regressions.

comments: It's commit status not actions' special feature.

> It's commit status not actions' special feature.

Reasonable answer. But, if click details, you will get 404 page. 
![image](https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/assets/18380374/c481e6ea-a470-46b4-9c36-4e834cd84a1a)
Should we hidden this when using Gitea action and user have no unit permission?

> > It's commit status not actions' special feature.
> 
> Reasonable answer. But, if click details, you will get 404 page. ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/18380374/262837534-c481e6ea-a470-46b4-9c36-4e834cd84a1a.png) Should we hidden this when using Gitea action and user have no unit permission?

Wow, I have no idea how to handle now.
I encountered a similar issue. If the repo's action unit is disabled, even though I'm a repo administrator, I'll still get a 404 page when clicking the "Details" link
I think this should be hidden when user does not have permission or the unit is disabled.
But you don't know if the commit status comes from actions or external sites.

> But you don't know if the commit status comes from actions or external sites.

Maybe we can check the `TargetURL` of a commit status. If a status comes from Gitea Actions, its `TargetURL` should have a prefix like `/{owner}/{repo}/actions`

Actually, I noticed another related issue.
If user has no access to code unit, but have access to action unit, 
you would see the workflow file name, branch name, commit id and so on.
And they also have links which will get 404.

review_comments: Is `TargetURL` a relative path or a URL?

It depends on the source of the commit status. 
- If the commit status comes from Gitea Actions, the `TargetURL` will be a relative path like `/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs/1/jobs/2`. 
- If the commit status comes from an external service like Drone, the `TargetURL` will be a URL.
